title: Gold Investment on Dhanteras 2026: Physical Gold or Gold ETFs?
description: Dhanteras is a traditional occasion for buying gold, but choosing the right investment vehicle is crucial for tax efficiency. Physical gold attracts 3% GST on.

faq.q: Is it always better to buy Gold ETFs than physical gold for investment?
faq.a: For pure investment purposes, Gold ETFs generally offer better liquidity, lower overall costs (no GST, lower expense ratios than making charges), and more favourable tax treatment due to a shorter LTCG holding period. Physical gold is often preferred for traditional, cultural, or consumption-related reasons.

faq.q: Do I have to pay GST when selling physical gold?
faq.a: No, GST is applicable only on the purchase of physical gold, not on its sale. However, capital gains tax will apply to your profits.

faq.q: How is indexation benefit calculated for capital gains on gold?
faq.a: Indexation adjusts the purchase price of your gold investment for inflation using the Cost Inflation Index (CII) notified by the Income Tax Department. This increases your effective purchase price, thereby reducing your taxable capital gain.

faq.q: Are Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) a better option than Gold ETFs?
faq.a: Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) offer an additional interest income (2.5% per annum) and are exempt from capital gains tax if held till maturity (8 years). They generally offer superior tax benefits compared to Gold ETFs, but come with a longer lock-in period.

faq.q: What documents are required to invest in Gold ETFs?
faq.a: To invest in Gold ETFs, you need a Demat account and a trading account with a SEBI-registered stockbroker. You will also need to complete KYC (Know Your Customer) formalities, which typically require identity and address proof.

faq.q: Can I convert my Gold ETF units into physical gold?
faq.a: While Gold ETFs are backed by physical gold, direct conversion of small units into physical gold is generally not practical for retail investors. This option is usually available for large institutional investors.

faq.q: What are the risks associated with Gold ETFs?
faq.a: Gold ETFs are subject to market risks, meaning their value can fluctuate with the price of gold. Other risks include tracking error (the fund not perfectly matching gold prices) and liquidity risk (difficulty selling units in low trading volumes).
